chunks: Ibn Muskan narrated from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about a man who performs the hajj on behalf of his brother, or his father, or on behalf of another man among the people: should he say anything?

He said: “Yes. At the time of his ihram, after he enters ihram, he should say: ‘O Allah, whatever fatigue, hardship, affliction, or dishevelment befalls me in this journey of mine, then grant so-and-so its reward in it, and reward me in my performing it on his behalf.’”

key_terms.إِحْرَامِهِ: the state of consecration in which this supplication is to be said
key_terms.بَلَاءٍ: trial or affliction faced during the pilgrimage
key_terms.سَفَرِي: the journey of pilgrimage during which hardship is endured
key_terms.شَعَثٍ: dishevelment and physical roughness resulting from travel and worship
key_terms.شِدَّةٍ: hardship or difficulty encountered on the journey
key_terms.قَضَائِي: my fulfillment of the act on behalf of another
key_terms.نَصَبٍ: fatigue or exertion experienced in travel
key_terms.ٱلْحَجَّ: the hajj being performed on behalf of another person

ai.seo_question: What should someone say when performing hajj on behalf of another person?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches a recommended supplication for one performing hajj on behalf of another person. It shows that the hardship endured in the journey may be dedicated in reward to the person for whom the hajj is being fulfilled, while the performer also seeks reward for carrying out the duty on that person's behalf.
